title: Consent for Lameness Examination With Nerve Blocks
body:
Sample Equine Clinic. This is a fictional sample form for demonstration only.

## The procedure
To find the source of your horse's lameness, the vet will watch it walk and trot, perform flexion tests, and then inject local anaesthetic near specific nerves or into a joint. If the lameness improves after a block, the problem is likely in the area that was numbed. Several blocks may be needed, and the exam can take a few hours. X-rays or ultrasound may be recommended afterwards.

## Risks
The skin is clipped and cleaned before each injection, but any injection carries a small risk of infection, which in a joint can be serious. Other risks include swelling, temporary soreness, and a brief loss of feeling that can make the horse unsteady. A light sedative may be needed for safety, and your vet will explain its risks.

## Your responsibilities
Please tell us about previous injuries, joint injections, or medication given in the last two weeks. Keep the injection sites clean and dry for 24 hours, keep the horse in a clean stable overnight, and call us straight away if you notice heat, swelling, or worsening lameness.

## Consent
By signing, I confirm that I own or am authorised to act for this horse, that I have read or listened to this form, and that I agree to the examination and nerve blocks described.
